title: Who decides if a ball is unplayable?
question: If your ball ends up in a really tough spot, like under a tree, who is allowed to declare it unplayable?
explanation: Only the player can decide if their ball is unplayable, no one else can make this decision for them.

juniorVersion.title: Who can say their ball can’t be played?
juniorVersion.question: If your ball goes somewhere really tricky, like under a bush, who gets to say 'I can’t play that ball'?

choices.text: The person you are playing against (your opponent)

juniorVersion.explanation: Only you, the player, can decide if your ball can’t be played. No one else can choose for you.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When you think you can’t hit your ball because it’s in a very hard place, like under a tree or bush.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Give children a plastic ball and ask them to roll it under a chair—let them decide if they could play it or need to call it unplayable.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think the referee or another player can make their ball unplayable for them.
